gaps.why_now: The first honest Phase 14 landing is a dedicated build gate that keeps the workqueue boundary-map slice reviewable without pretending Zigux already owns live async execution.
A dedicated make target keeps the Phase 14 survey lane runnable with the same bounded discipline as the earlier tranche gates.
The existing export shim proves Zigux already has a reviewable kernel namespace foothold, so the workqueue lane can add a pure boundary map without inventing a fresh top-level layout.

The first honest `workqueue_bridge.zig` foothold is a boundary map around `queue_work_on()`, `__queue_work()`, `__alloc_workqueue()`, `cancel_work_sync()`, `manage_workers()`, and the rescuer or scheduler hooks, with explicit stay-in-C decisions where concurrency ownership is still too coupled to `worker_pool` state.
A dedicated Phase 14 gate is the smallest truthful way to lock the new boundary-map descriptor to the manifest and keep later runs from drifting into fake implementation claims.
The slice note records the exact boundary-map posture so the lane does not overstate symbol cataloging as a workqueue helper or execution bridge.
The survey note compares the 8,439-line `kernel/workqueue.c` anchor and its supporting header or test surfaces against the new boundary map so future runs stay honest about what still belongs in C.

The bridge now carries a small concurrency audit outline around `manage_workers()`, `struct worker_pool`, `wq_worker_running()` or `wq_worker_sleeping()`, and `rescuer_thread()` so Zigux can name `pool->manager`, forward-progress fields, scheduler-visible running state, and `pwq->mayday_cursor` without claiming live execution ownership.

The bridge now records the `__queue_work()` gate that chooses between `pool->worklist` and `pwq->inactive_works` while `max_active` and ordered-workqueue sequencing are still enforced under `pool->lock`, which is a reviewable field-level audit step before any wrapper claims live enqueue ownership. The same boundary keeps later `workqueue_set_max_active()` tuning honest by naming the inactive-list seam without moving it out of C.

The bridge now records the `__queue_work()` last-pool reentrancy handoff, the `process_one_work()` unlock and relock execution window, and the `worker_thread()` idle sleep transition so Zigux can name where `last_pool->lock`, `pool->lock`, and TASK_IDLE handoffs stay under C-owned concurrency control.

The next honest Phase 14 step is to audit `try_to_grab_pending()`, `queue_work_on()`, and the unbound `__queue_work()` `pwq->refcnt` retry path so Zigux can name pending ownership, retry, and reselection rules without claiming live submission control.

Live worker_pool execution, pool draining, hotplug transitions, scheduler callbacks, rescue behavior, and forward-progress correctness remain blocked until the boundary map grows a tighter concurrency audit and Phase 14 still keeps those mechanisms in the existing C implementation.
